a1
Abraham died at a good old age. Isaac and Ishmael buried him beside Sarah.
a2
Isaac prayed for his wife Rebekah, who had no child, and the Lord answered.
b1
Rebekah carried twins who struggled in her womb. The Lord told her: two nations are in you, and the older will serve the younger.
b2
The first was red and hairy, Esau. The second came holding his heel, Jacob.
c1
Esau became a hunter. Jacob stayed among the tents. Isaac loved Esau, and Rebekah loved Jacob.
d1
One day Esau came in from the field, exhausted. He saw Jacob's red stew: give me some, he said.
d2
Jacob said: first sell me your birthright. Esau said: I am about to die, what use is it to me?
e1
He swore, and sold it. Jacob gave him bread and lentil stew. Esau ate and walked away, despising his birthright.
h1
Esau did not lose his birthright to an enemy. He traded it for one meal.
h2
The text says he despised it, trading the future for a moment.
h3
What God gives is worth more than what we crave right now.
h4
Ask yourself: what am I trading away?
i
What lasting thing are you trading for comfort?
